item.title: The Way Back
item.description: Later that day Gever and Lee decided to explore the right side of the clearcut, accessible from the top of the glassing hill, through an old logging road that cut between the alders and spruce trees but was narrowed enough to not allow a truck to pass.
item.dc:creator: André Amnc
item.content:encoded:
Later that day Gever and Lee decided to explore the right side of the clearcut, accessible from the top of the glassing hill, through an old logging road that cut between the alders and spruce trees but was narrowed enough to not allow a truck to pass. They had passed the first hours of the afternoon walking around the treeline overlooking the south side of that hill’s face, looking for scat, marks, anything that would tell if they were investing in the right place. So, figuring they were just collecting miles under their boots, they decided to head back to the glassing spot. “I wonder if we are going to find bears, any bears. We’ve been short of opportunities these days.” - Commented Lee, while stopping at a creek to fill up his water bladder. “I don’t know. Matt and I have been here during the last summer and man, this place is bear heaven.” - Gever responded, quietly, a few paces ahead. “From that glassing spot back there we’ve seen bear after bear, after bear... after bear.” - He added. “Ah yeah, you guys mentioned it before. I think its too soon then, there are a lot of berry patches, I’ve seen”. Lee said. “Perhaps, still the first weeks of the season and it is not hot enough yet, definitely not for berries”. Gever said. “You’ve been hunting for awhile now, haven’t you?” - He asked Lee. “I have, three years so far.” - He responded, getting up and shacking his pack to adjust its weight on his hips. “I guess, we’ve all started late in life, I am already 36. So we have to learn mostly by ourselves.” He said. “It’s good that we found this group, we can share, mostly the experiences and the fun. Man, I want to bring my son with me when he gets a tad bigger.” Lee said with a smile under his beard. They slowed their decent back over the logging road to a slow stride, still careful enough to check for sign. “You bet, I don’t know if I would be hunting if it weren’t for this crew, specially Matt.” Gever concurred. “Actually I know I would take at least twice as much time to even get comfortable about camping by myself in the woods.” Gever added. “Alright, you afraid of being by yourself in the wilderness, aye?” - Lee pointed. “Pretty much. I have no qualms with it while with one or more people though, even unarmed.” He answered. “I am not troubled of walking the woods by myself either if I know that on the other side I will meet with someone. It’s just... I don’t know, its a fear.” Lee turned halfway towards him and looking him in the eye: “There is no problem with that, I had a thing too with this fear, but I was younger and I think this makes it easier.” Lee said calmly. “When you are a kid its easier to commit to stupid things.” He laughed with gusto. “I guess.” Gever said, laughing a bit too. “But its a time thing. I had it too for awhile while going solo hunting a couple of times.” Lee mentioned. “That’s another beast to tame, who are you when its only you there.” “Exactly, you got to trust your gut a lot more, don’t you? I mean, any situation its not like you will have the answers right away.” Gever nodded. “But I am pushing closer to my forties, I feel I am missing a lot.” He concluded. “Yeah, man, FOMO is a real bitch, ain’t it?” Lee said gargling with that bushy santa claus beard.

A few paces ahead they spot a black mass on the side of the road, a bear scat the hunting buddies missed on their way up. It wasn’t far from the turn into the narrow winding washed road down to the glassing spot. It looked fresh, perhaps a couple of days old. “Hey, I have an idea. Do you want to have some fun?” Lee asked Gever. “What?” He interjected. “I have a contractors bag in my pack, we can pick up this poop and place it by Matt’s tent over the night. Think of it man, it would be hilarious”. He laughed hard! “We haven’t been seeing much sign lately, I mean, bears even less. Can you imagine Matt’s face when he steps out of this tent in the morning and there is a huge dump right by it?” He added. “Indeed man, that would be amazing. I can even imagine he screaming “WTH”, that grumpy old man.” Gever laughed. Lee opened his pack and took a black bag out, flipped it inside out and put one hand inside it. “Let’s go!” He exclaimed. He touched that soft pile that started to loosen up in a wet paste. “Oh man, this is so disgusting!” Laughing and making gagging sounds. Gever was rolling on his belly laughing so hard he was crying. “Dude, come’on it will stink your pack hard!” He said. “No shit it will.” Lee responded laughing. “Get another back in my pack, lets double wrap this sucker.” He asked his hunting buddy. Gever opened the bag and waited for Lee to finish the dirty job. Like dog’s poop he reversed the bag onto itself and put a knot in it, then threw it inside the other bag. Gever closed that one and did a weight check. “That is much shit!” He said like someone weighing gold in old stories.

Lee put the memento in his pack, closed it and before he finished getting up Gever’s radio cracked. “Bud, you listening?” Matt’s voice coming out of the radio. “Yes, man. We are listening.” He checked. “I am at the road up of the glassing spot, come quick, I’ve found a bear!”. The laughing stopped and both exchanged a stern glance.
